served.stem: Salicylaldehyde (shown) has an intramolecular hydrogen bond between its phenol O-H and the adjacent aldehyde oxygen. Compared with the IR of a simple phenol, what is the expected effect of this intramolecular hydrogen bonding on the O-H stretch?
choices: The O-H stretch becomes a sharp doublet, much like the two N-H bands of a primary aromatic amine
The O-H band moves to ~2250 cm-1, overlapping the nitrile region
The O-H stretch sharpens and shifts to HIGHER wavenumber (above 3600 cm-1)
The O-H stretch disappears entirely from the spectrum once the internal hydrogen bond forms
The O-H stretch is broadened and shifted to LOWER wavenumber (below ~3200 cm-1)
served.bankWhy: Hydrogen bonding weakens the O-H bond, lowering its frequency and broadening the band. The intramolecular H-bond in salicylaldehyde persists even when dilute, so O-H is broad and shifted to lower wavenumber vs a free O-H (~3600).

bank.keyText: The O-H stretch is broadened and shifted to LOWER wavenumber (below ~3200 cm-1)

answer.text: The O-H stretch is broadened and shifted to LOWER wavenumber (below ~3200 cm-1)
answer.line: The H-bond pulls on the hydrogen and weakens the O-H bond. A weaker bond vibrates lower, and a spread of strengths smears the band broad.

steps: Picture the ring. The phenol H reaches over to the aldehyde O and closes a six-membered ring, and that hold stays even in dilute solution.
Ask what a hold does to a bond. Sharing the H with a second oxygen weakens the O-H bond, and a weaker bond vibrates at lower wavenumber.
The hold is never one fixed strength, so the band smears out. Broad and low, below about 3200, instead of sharp near 3600.

choices.text: The O-H stretch becomes a sharp doublet, much like the two N-H bands of a primary aromatic amine
choices.note: Two sharp bands belong to an NH2 group, two N-H bonds stretching together and apart. An O-H has one H, so it gives one band.

choices.text: The O-H band moves to ~2250 cm-1, overlapping the nitrile region
choices.note: Near 2250 is where C-N and C-C triple bonds absorb. An H-bond lowers the O-H stretch, but nowhere near that far.

choices.text: The O-H stretch sharpens and shifts to HIGHER wavenumber (above 3600 cm-1)
choices.note: Sharp and above 3600 is a free O-H, one with no H-bond, as in a dilute simple phenol. Bonding sends the band the other way.

choices.text: The O-H stretch disappears entirely from the spectrum once the internal hydrogen bond forms
choices.note: The band moves and spreads, sometimes under the C-H bands, but the O-H bond is still there and still absorbs.

choices.text: The O-H stretch is broadened and shifted to LOWER wavenumber (below ~3200 cm-1)
choices.note: Broad and below 3200: the signature of an O-H held by a hydrogen bond.
